title: Counting digits is a logarithm
hook: Double a number 100 times. It explodes, but its digit count marches in a straight line.

knows: place value: each extra digit is ten times bigger
doesNotKnow: that log10 of a number is about its digit count

misconception: A number that doubles 100 times has around 100 digits, or its digit count is unpredictable.
objective: The learner can explain that because 2^10 = 1024 is about 1000, every 10 doublings add about 3 digits, so 2^100 has 31 digits; the steady growth of the digit count is what a base-10 logarithm measures.

claims.source: Exact BigInt arithmetic in node: (1n << 100n).toString() has length 31. The stage computes the same value the same way.

claims.text: After 10, 20, ..., 100 doublings the number has 4, 7, 10, ..., 31 digits: each 10 doublings add exactly 3 digits in this range.
claims.source: Digits of 2^(10k) = floor(10k x 0.30103) + 1 = 3k + 1 for k = 1..10 (and up to k = 33). Recomputed with BigInt in node: 4,7,10,13,16,19,22,25,28,31.

claims.text: log10(2^100) = 100 x log10(2) = 100 x 0.301, about 30.1; a whole number's digit count is the whole part of its base-10 logarithm plus one.
claims.source: log10(2) = 0.30103 (node Math.log10). A number N with d digits satisfies 10^(d-1) <= N < 10^d, so d = floor(log10 N) + 1.

recall.question: Roughly how many digits does 2^50 have (2 doubled 50 times)?
recall.why: Every 10 doublings multiply by about 1000, adding 3 digits: 1 + 5 x 3 = 16. (2^50 = 1,125,899,906,842,624.)
